LESSON: VEGETATION IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Vegetation in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Vegetation in Eastern Africa, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: where How can we conserve vegetation in our environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Vegetation in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: Learners show hard work as they plant and care for vegetation school.

• Peace: Learners respect self and others as they discuss, in groups to describe the characteristics of the main types of vegetation in

Eastern Africa.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PICs):

● Environmental education: learners practise environmental awareness as they plan and write down, in groups, how they will

conserve vegetation within the school compound.

● Patriotism: learners demonstrate patriotism as they plan and carry out activities on conservation of vegetation in their locality.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Agriculture and Nutrition: learners relate to skills learnt in Agriculture and Nutrition as they plant and care for vegetation at school.

• Creative arts: learners apply skills learnt Creative Arts as they draw and display in class a map indicating the main types of

vegetation in Eastern Africa.

Suggested Learning Resources

Local and extended environment, print and electronic maps, photographs and pictures, internet sources ,vetted digital resources,
